title: Pedro Henrique da Costa Avelar
text:
Biography
Pedro is interested in developing causal representation learning and neuro-symbolic methods to improve the generalisability, fairness, and interpretability of medical AI. His past experience includes using Graph Neural Networks and Transformers for symbolic problems and computer vision, multi-omics integration and prior-knowledge-based omics analysis, and analysing biases in Machine Translation.

title: Steph Riley
text:
Biography
Steph’s research interests are in causal inference methods to address generalisability and transportability problems in treatment effect estimation and prediction models, to support fair and equitable healthcare. She also enjoys survival analysis, particularly competing risks and multistate models.

title: Siân Bladon
text:
Biography
I am an experienced health data scientist currently working as a Lecturer in Health Data Sciences within the Division of Informatics, Imaging and Data Science at the University of Manchester. I previously worked as a PDRA on the CONNECT project, developing a clinical prediction model to predict the risk of relapse in people with psychosis using data collected through wearable devices and smartphones. My current research interests focus on addressing the challenges of incorporating high-frequency data (e.g. from wearable devices) into clinical prediction models. I teach primarily on the MSc Health Data Science and Health Informatics programmes, contributing to teaching on statistics, data visualisation, data linkage and digital transformation.
